fas_summary: Frederick County Council approved Ordinance 26-01-001 creating a 2,614-acre Critical Digital Infrastructure Overlay Zone (CDI-OZ) near Adamstown, designating areas where data centers may be located and concentrating development around an existing data center campus. Residents organized the Frederick County Data Center Referendum Committee, collected 21,029 valid signatures (exceeding the required 15,611), and the Board of Elections certified the petition on April 3, 2026 — placing a referendum on the November 2026 ballot to overturn the ordinance. If voters reject it, the 2,600-acre overlay zone would be invalidated.

fas_summary: Follows Phase 1 by establishing new use-specific zoning standards for data centers and utility substations, including noise regulations, building height rules, onsite power generation and energy storage requirements, and compatibility standards. Research and draft text amendments were underway October 2025 through April 2026.

fas_ordinance: Voter-Approved Ballot Measure on Data Center Tax Incentives
fas_summary: Port Washington voters approved (66% in favor) a ballot measure requiring that any tax incentives offered to data center developers must first receive voter approval before taking effect. Represents one of the first enacted local ballot measures in the U.S. to directly constrain a local government's ability to offer data center tax incentives without public consent. A parallel measure in Janesville, Wisconsin is under consideration that would require voter approval for any data center project exceeding $450 million.
